subjective.citation_text: Patient: I'm 82 years old, and I'm a male. I'm here because I had an acute on chronic heart failure exacerbation, and I was in the hospital for a few days. I felt really bad with shortness of breath and swelling in my ankles, and I even had to call 911. But now I feel much better. Doctor: Could you please provide more details about your current symptoms and how long you've been experiencing them? Patient: Sure, doc. The swelling in my ankles has been going on for a while, but it got worse before I went to the hospital. And the shortness of breath came on pretty suddenly—one day I was fine, and the next I was struggling to breathe. I had to call 911, and they gave me that special mask to help me breathe. But since I've been home, I haven't had any trouble breathing or swelling anymore. I feel good now. Doctor: Could you please provide details about any prior heart failure diagnoses, medications you were taking during your hospitalization, and any previous hospitalizations related to heart failure or other conditions? Patient: I was told I have chronic kidney disease and hypertension, and this was the first time I had an acute heart failure episode. During the hospital stay, they gave me some medications, including a water pill that made me go to the bathroom a lot, and some blood pressure meds. I don't remember the exact names, but I'm taking them now as prescribed. I haven't been hospitalized for heart failure before, but I have had some issues with my kidneys. Doctor: Could you please provide the specific names and dosages of the medications you are currently taking, including the diuretic and blood pressure medications? Patient: I'm taking Bumex, which is the water pill, and I think it's two milligrams once a day. For my blood pressure, I'm on Cozaar and Norvasc, but I don't remember the exact dosages. The doctor told me to keep taking them, so I do. Doctor: Could you
